transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No — stop using the hob now, including the unaffected zones, and isolate it at the cooker switch or consumer unit if you can do so safely. A crack through a ceramic hob can let spills or cleaning moisture reach electrical parts underneath, creating a shock or short-circuit/fire risk. This is most consistent with impact damage to the ceramic/glass top rather than a heating-zone fault. Do not put tape, sealant or a cover over the crack, and avoid cleaning it with liquid until it has been repaired or replaced. It needs assessment by a qualified appliance engineer. Depending on the make and model, the glass top may or may not be economically replaceable; often the complete hob is replaced.
Ok, that's fair. There's a red switch on the wall labelled cooker, so I can turn it off there. Some pasta water spilled earlier and might have gone into the crack. Is that a worry?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Yes, it is a concern. Salted pasta water is conductive, so if any has entered the crack it may have reached parts below the ceramic surface. Even if the hob appears to work, it must not be used again until a qualified appliance engineer has assessed it. Turn the cooker isolation switch off and leave it off. Do not try to switch the hob back on to see whether it has dried out, and do not remove covers or attempt to dry inside it. Once isolated, leave the surface alone to dry naturally; avoid adding any more water or cleaner around the crack. The most likely issue remains the impact-cracked ceramic top, but the spill means there is also a possible electrical contamination/moisture issue underneath. An engineer will need to inspect it before it can be considered safe.

claimsRejected.claim: The fact that the ring still heats does not make it safe.

plan: They asked: "Can I keep using it until I get a new one?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "Crack across the front left ring after a cast iron pan was dropped on it". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
